newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: CSM sees ingredients driving growth.
newsitem.headline: CSM sees ingredients driving growth.

text.p: Strong growth in CSM's food ingredients division will continue to drive turnover and profit increases at the Dutch food group, the company said on Tuesday.
"The turnover and profits of the ingredients division will continue to grow strongly," chairman Gerard van Loon said at the presentation of the company's 1995/96 annual report.
"Overall, we expect CSM's net earnings and cash flow per share to show a further rise in the current financial year."

Van Loon said turnover in the ingredients division was seen increasing by around 500 million guilders to 1.6 billion in the 1996/97 financial year to September 30, a rise of 45 percent compared to a year-earlier 32.4 percent improvement.
Besides autonomous growth, acquisitions would again be a major factor, he said.
Further acquisitions would most likely be smaller "add-ons" to existing businesses, Van Loon said, unless an outstanding larger opportunity presented itself.
CSM expects its sugar division to continue contributing good profits, although it is not expected to grow given the regulated market in which it operates.
Turnover and profits of the company's food division would also increase once the intended acquisition of Scandinavian sweets maker Malaco, announced in June, had been concluded, Van Loon said.
The acquisition had yet to be finalised owing to the "legalistic" attitude of the Norwegian authorities, he said, but CSM hoped to conclude the deal within a few months.
Turnover in the food division was seen increasing to around 1.4 billion guilders in the 1996/97 financial year from 1.3 billion, Van Loon said.
